title: 2 Free Self-Hosted Tools to Automate a Business Workflow with AI
content:
Most small businesses pay for 5 different SaaS tools
just to move data from one place to another.
You might NOT need any of them.
Today I'll show you 2 free tools you can SELF-HOST
that can automate a real business workflow with AI.
No expensive subscription.
And stay till the end,
because the last part is where most people get it WRONG.
Tool number 1 is n8n.
n8n is a workflow automation tool.
Think of it like a visual flowchart.
Something happens, like a new form entry or a new email,
and n8n runs a chain of steps for you.
The big deal is that you can SELF-HOST it.
The free Community edition runs on your own server or laptop,
so your data stays with you.
Quick note: n8n calls its license fair-code,
so read the license before you resell it.
Tool number 2 is Ollama.
Ollama is open-source.
It lets you run open AI models LOCALLY on your own machine.
So instead of paying per request to a cloud API,
the model runs on your hardware.
And n8n can talk to it.
Now here's where it gets interesting.
Let's put them together.
Imagine you run a small agency.
Every day, leads come in through a website form.
Someone on your team reads each one,
decides if it's a real lead,
and copies it into a spreadsheet.
That's boring, repetitive work.
Say you build this instead.
Step 1. The form sends the lead to an n8n webhook.
Step 2. n8n sends the message to a local model running in Ollama,
with a simple prompt:
classify this lead as hot, warm or cold, and write a 1 line summary.
Step 3. n8n writes the result into your sheet or CRM.
Step 4. If the lead is HOT, n8n pings your team on chat.
That's 1 workflow.
No new SaaS bill.
And your customer data never leaves your own setup.
But here's the part most people get wrong.
They try to automate EVERYTHING on day 1.
Don't do that.
Pick ONE workflow that eats at least 1 hour of your week.
Automate only that.
Keep a human checking the output for the first 2 weeks.
Then expand.
Also be honest about the trade-off.
Self-hosting means YOU maintain it.
Updates, backups, and a machine strong enough to run the model.
For a small team, that's usually worth it.
For a team with zero tech support, a hosted plan might be easier.
Here's my take.
The skill companies will pay for is not knowing 50 AI tools.
It's looking at a messy business process
and turning it into 1 clean, reliable workflow.
That's exactly what an AI solutions engineer does.
